def: properly, to adjure, i.e. (usually in a bad sense) imprecate

words.word: from thee about which thou cursedst
upon him to cause him to swear
upon him to make him swear

occurrences.text: And he said unto his mother, The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from thee, about which thou cursedst, and spakest of also in mine ears, behold, the silver is with me; I took it. And his mother said, Blessed be thou of the Lord, my son.
words: from thee about which thou cursedst

occurrences.text: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.
If any man trespass against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to swear, and the oath come before thine altar in this house:
words: upon him to cause him to swear

occurrences.text: If a man sin against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to make him swear, and the oath come before thine altar in this house;
words: upon him to make him swear

occurrences.text: By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.
They have spoken words, swearing falsely in making a covenant: thus judgment springeth up as hemlock in the furrows of the field.
